Legacy FORCE_CLI cleanup

How the gateway removes the CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI value older releases exported.

About 5 min read

An older gateway also exported CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI=1, which pushed durable chats and SSH rows through the adapter as extra local app-servers. Registration, including the unified service's re-registration at start and the login agent, and gateway desktop unregister remove a value of 1 from the login session only when it is provably the gateway's. Two things prove it, and every command needs both: the registration receipt must name a wrapper, and the session's CODEX_CLI_PATH must name a gateway wrapper.

Command Receipt CODEX_CLI_PATH must equal
gateway desktop register names a wrapper the receipt's wrapper, the wrapper this registration installs, or an older wrapper in this gateway's state directory
gateway desktop unregister names a wrapper the receipt's wrapper or an older wrapper in this gateway's state directory
gateway desktop status (legacyForceCli) names a wrapper the receipt's wrapper or an older wrapper in this gateway's state directory

The older-wrapper case is the common upgrade case: newer code writes a wrapper with a new content hash, the receipt names that one, and the login session still holds the older wrapper the previous registration set. A path counts as such a wrapper only when it is an absolute, normalised path naming a regular file owned by you, or a missing entry, directly in the gateway state directory, whose name is exactly desktop-wrapper- plus 16 lowercase hex digits. A look-alike stays foreign: the same name in another directory or a subdirectory of the state directory, a name with a suffix, a shorter, non-hex, or uppercase suffix, a path that climbs back through .. or ends in a slash, or a name held by a symlink or a directory. The gateway desktop launcher runs the inherited CODEX_CLI_PATH through the same path test in src/desktop-wrapper-path.ts, or accepts the exact wrapper it is about to launch, and stops there: it never stats the entry, so an accepted name is proof enough for it. That check has one effect, which is to drop a legacy CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI=1 from the single app process the launcher starts; it changes nothing in the login session. Registration refuses a foreign value instead of replacing it, unregister leaves it alone, and registration never deletes a stale wrapper file. If a foreign CODEX_CLI_PATH override blocks registration, run launchctl unsetenv CODEX_CLI_PATH and then register again.

The receipt requirement is what turns a missing receipt into a refusal rather than a guess. Where the receipt was cleared or never written, a gateway wrapper path beside a 1 proves the path is ours but says nothing about who exported the pair: gateway desktop register refuses with a message that names the variable and the remedy, never a value, saying that CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI is set to the legacy value, and gateway desktop status reports legacyForceCli: false. gateway desktop unregister still clears an own CODEX_CLI_PATH there, because that path is ours whether or not the receipt survived, and it leaves the 1 alone; when it does, it reports legacyForceCliKept: true so the cleared path and the kept value show up in one output, and gateway uninstall passes that flag through. gateway desktop status also reports staleWrapper: true while the session points at a wrapper of ours that the receipt no longer names; that alone is not an active adapter, so activeForFutureLaunches stays false until a registration writes the current wrapper. Alongside legacyForceCli, status reports forceCliSet, which reads the variable with launchctl getenv, removes exactly one trailing newline, and counts it as set when anything remains, so a whitespace-only value is set; it never carries the value itself. If launchctl cannot be run or times out, register, unregister and status fail with that error rather than treating the variable as unset, so forceCliSet: false is only ever reported on a successful read. gateway desktop only leaves an inherited 1 out of the app it launches, and only when the inherited CODEX_CLI_PATH names a gateway wrapper by that spelling test; it does not change the login session, so later Dock launches still see it.

After installing a release that stops setting it, clear the old value first, then restart the app:

  1. Run gateway desktop register. This works for both the unified service and a standalone desktop LaunchAgent. Do not wait for the unified service to clear it on its own: the supervisor moves to a new release when it is fully idle, with no app connected and no chat loaded, or, after 15 minutes of waiting, once it is quiet (no turn running, no background terminal and no turn ended in the last 5 minutes; see docs/services.md), so with ChatGPT open and busy it can wait a long time. Quitting ChatGPT lets it go idle and restart, and a standalone LaunchAgent also clears it at the next login.
  2. If registration refuses because no receipt proves the value, clear it yourself and register again: launchctl unsetenv CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI. That is the whole remedy for the missing-receipt case; nothing else in the gateway touches the value without a receipt naming a wrapper.
  3. Run gateway desktop status and confirm forceCliSet: false, not only legacyForceCli: false. A value that is not ours also reads legacyForceCli: false, while forceCliSet: false is the proof that no CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI is left in the session at all.
  4. Quit and reopen ChatGPT once. Reopening earlier keeps the old behavior, including the repeated "409 Remote app server already online" errors.
